You are building a reusable citation tool for a Ramp deployment pipeline in /home/user/Genera.

# YOU OWN EXACTLY ONE FILE
- /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/cite.py

Do NOT create or edit anything else. Another agent is writing a different script and the parent is editing SKILL.md and AUDIT_PATTERNS.md concurrently. Do not git commit or push.

# WHY THIS EXISTS

The pipeline emits a customer-facing `audit_log.json`. Every citation in it must be verifiable without opening the source file, and `scripts/check_audit_style.py` (read it first) GATES this: a citation must name a real packet file, contain a verbatim quoted span of 15+ characters, and carry attribution — a speaker name or a row/line locator. A bare timestamp is explicitly not enough.

Today that gate exists with no tool behind it. Running two packets, throwaway citation helpers were written twice from scratch and thrown away. A fresh session facing an unseen packet would write a third. Your script is the permanent version.

Read these first:
- /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/check_audit_style.py  (the gate you must satisfy — especially its citation check and its `norm()` folding)
- /home/user/Genera/.claude/skills/ramp-deployment/scripts/check_quotes.py       (house style: shebang, docstring with usage, module constants, `arg()` helper, `main()` returning an exit code, `sys.exit(main())`)
- /home/user/Genera/out/client_a_acme_corp/audit_log.json  and  /home/user/Genera/out/client_c_apex_health/audit_log.json  (the citation format you must reproduce — look at `assumptions_made[].source`)
- ALL FIVE packets under /home/user/Genera/candidate/customer_packets/ — the formats differ and that is the whole problem.

Repo root is `parents[4]` from the scripts directory. Resolve from `__file__`, never cwd. Support `--repo` override.

# THE FORMAT TO PRODUCE

Transcript with speakers:
```
discovery_call_01.txt — Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp), [05:41], <context>: "<verbatim quote>"
```
Structured/line-addressed file:
```
department_roster.csv, row 15 — <context>: "<verbatim row>"
security_requirements.doc, line 16 — <context>: "<verbatim quote>"
```
The `<context>` is a human-written clause the caller supplies. Everything else you derive from the file.

# CLI

```
python3 cite.py --packet <packet_name> --quote "<verbatim text>" [--context "<clause>"] [--repo <path>]
python3 cite.py --packet <packet_name> --speakers        # show the speaker map you detected
```

- `--quote`: locate this text across every file in the packet and emit the citation. Match after the same whitespace/unicode folding `check_audit_style.py` uses, so a quote typed with ASCII punctuation still finds curly-quoted source. Print the citation to stdout.
- If the quote appears in more than one file, or more than once, say so and show each with its location rather than silently picking one.
- If not found, exit 1 with a clear message. Never invent a citation.
- `--speakers`: print the detected speaker map so a human can sanity-check the parse before trusting 30 citations built on it.
- Also expose the same functionality as importable functions (`cite(packet, quote, context)`), since the agent driving the pipeline will import it rather than shell out 35 times.

# THE HARD PART: FORMATS DIFFER, AND THE NEXT PACKET IS UNSEEN

You must handle the five packets present AND degrade sensibly on a format nobody has seen. Study the real files before designing.

Known shapes:
1. `client_a_acme_corp/discovery_call_01.txt` and `client_c_apex_health/discovery_call_apex.txt` — an "Attendees:" block mapping full names and roles to initials, then turns like `[00:47] DM: ...`. Parse the attendee block to expand `DM` into `Diane Marsh (VP Finance, Acme Corp)`.
2. `client_d_hypergrowth/slack_export_finance.txt` — turns like `[2026-08-05 16:40] rachel.kim: ...`. No attendee block. Derive a display name from the handle.
3. `client_d_hypergrowth/fragmented_notes_feb2026.md` — markdown notes, little or no speaker structure. Fall back to line numbers.
4. `client_b_logistica_globex/*` — Spanish transcript and a numbered policy memo. The memo has section numbers (e.g. `5.3`); prefer a section locator over a bare line number when the line clearly sits under one.
5. `client_c_apex_health/security_requirements.doc` — a numbered requirements document; `.doc` extension but plain text.
6. `*.csv` — cite by row number, where row 1 is the header. Emit the whole row as the quote.

Design the detection so an unrecognised format still produces a VALID citation via the line-number fallback. Never fail merely because no speaker was found — a line locator satisfies the gate.

Where a document names an owner or approver in its header (packet C's `Document owner: M. Vance, Director of Compliance` and `approved by Risk Committee 2026-07-30`), include that as attribution alongside the line number. That is what makes a document citation as verifiable as a transcript one.

# QUALITY BAR
- Python 3, standard library only.
- Roughly 120-170 lines. This is the one script allowed to be a little longer than the 40-line guardrail, because it replaces work that is otherwise redone per packet — but keep each detector its own small function and keep it readable.
- Module docstring must explain WHY (the gate exists with no tool; helpers were rewritten per packet) not just how.

# TESTING (required — do not skip)
Test against REAL packet files and report actual output:
1. Packet A: quote `I never want to see a decline` → must attribute to Diane Marsh with role and timestamp.
2. Packet A: quote `Priya and me. And probably Sana in IT for the user-management side` → Diane Marsh, [05:41].
3. Packet A CSV: quote `Jenny Park` → must produce a `row 15` citation with the full row.
4. Packet C: quote `Category-level controls are NOT sufficient` → line citation naming M. Vance as document owner.
5. Packet D Slack: quote something real from `slack_export_finance.txt` → must attribute to the handle with its timestamp.
6. Packet D notes: quote something real from `fragmented_notes_feb2026.md` → line-number fallback, no crash.
7. Packet B: quote something real from the Spanish memo → confirm it does not crash on non-ASCII and produces a usable locator.
8. A quote that does not exist → exit 1, clear message, no fabricated output.
9. `--speakers` on packets A, C and D.
10. **Round-trip proof (the important one):** take the citations your script generates, drop them into a copy of a real audit_log.json under /tmp, and run `check_audit_style.py --repo` against it. Its `source citations` check must PASS. A citation tool whose output fails the citation gate is worthless — prove it does not.

Clean up anything created outside the repo.

In your final message report: the final line count, the exact citation string produced for tests 1-7, and the result of test 10.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Hold out/<packet>/audit_log.json to the standard the customer reads it at.
3	
4	The audit log is not an internal artifact: Acme Corp's finance team reads it verbatim, and
5	their review of the first packet raised three real defects. Each check exists so that
6	defect cannot ship again, on this packet or any other.
7	
8	  (a) pronouns  — "he should not see anyone else's spend" left the reviewer guessing who
9	                  "he" was. Name the person or the role, never a pronoun. One exception: a
10	                  `source` field carries a VERBATIM customer quote, and the customer's own
11	                  words are not ours to sanitize, so text inside quotation marks there is
12	                  exempt while everything around it is still checked.
13	  (b) jargon    — internal row IDs (CAP-*, DRIFT-*), pipeline vocabulary (req_id, archetype,
14	                  traceability, the capability ledger) and implementation slang ("fans out")
15	                  mean nothing to a customer and leak how the sausage is made. Banned
16	                  everywhere, quotes included.
17	  (c) citations — "discovery_call_01.txt — 'Priya and me.' [05:41]" was rejected as useless:
18	                  the reader cannot tell who "me" is or why that line supports the
19	                  assumption. A citation must name a real packet file, quote it verbatim at
20	                  useful length, and say who said it or where in the file it sits. A bare
21	                  timestamp is not attribution — that is the case the customer rejected.
22	  (d) ordering  — blocking flags come before non-blocking ones, so a reader who stops after
23	                  the first few has still seen everything that blocks go-live.
24	  (e) evidence  — an unsupported-API claim with undated evidence is unverifiable.
25	
26	  python3 check_audit_style.py --packet client_a_acme_corp [--repo /path/to/repo]
27	
28	Every check runs; all failures are reported. Exit 0 only if all five pass.
29	"""
30	import sys, json, re, pathlib, unicodedata
31	
32	ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]  # scripts/ -> ramp-deployment/ -> skills/ -> .claude/ -> repo root
33	ARRAYS = ("assumptions_made", "missing_information_flags", "conflicts", "unsupported_api_requests")
34	CITED = {"assumptions_made": ("source",), "conflicts": ("source_a", "source_b")}
35	PRONOUN = re.compile(r"\b(?:he|she|his|her|hers|him|they|them|their|theirs)\b", re.I)
36	# A quoted span. An apostrophe inside a word ("else's") must not close a single-quoted span.
37	QUOTED = re.compile(r"\"[^\"]*\"|(?<![A-Za-z])'.*?'(?![A-Za-z])", re.S)
38	JARGON = [re.compile(p, re.I) for p in (
39	    r"\bCAP-[A-Z][A-Z-]*", r"\bDRIFT-[A-Z][A-Z-]*", r"\breq_id\b",
40	    # This pipeline's own requirement ids are zero-padded to three digits (REQ-001), and
41	    # leaking one into a customer document is the defect. A customer's OWN numbering is
42	    # not: Apex Health Partners numbers its compliance requirements REQ-1..REQ-6 and
43	    # requires responses to cite them. Match only the padded form.
44	    r"\bREQ-\d{3,}\b",
45	    r"\barchetypes?\b", r"\btraceability\b", r"\bcapability ledger\b", r"\bthe ledger\b",
46	    r"\bfans out\b", r"\bfan[- ]out\b")]
47	SPEAKER = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][A-Za-z'-]+\b")       # Priya Shetty
48	LOCATOR = re.compile(r"\b(?:row|line)s?\s+\d+\b", re.I)          # row 12 / line 47
49	FILENAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{2,5}\b")
50	YEAR = re.compile(r"(?<!\d)(19|20)\d{2}(?!\d)")  # not \b\d{4}\b: that fires on 2026_08_30 and on 5000
51	FOLD = {"‘": "'", "’": "'", "‚": "'", "“": '"', "”": '"',
52	        "„": '"', "–": "-", "—": "-", "−": "-", "…": "..."}
53	
54	
55	def norm(text):
56	    """Fold unicode punctuation to ASCII and collapse whitespace. Case is preserved."""
57	    text = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", text)
58	    return " ".join("".join(FOLD.get(ch, ch) for ch in text).split())
59	
60	
61	def strings(audit):
62	    """Yield (array, index, field, value) for every string in the four audit arrays."""
63	    for name in ARRAYS:
64	        for i, entry in enumerate(audit.get(name) or []):
65	            for field, value in (entry or {}).items():
66	                if isinstance(value, str):
67	                    yield name, i, field, value
68	
69	
70	def unquoted(text):
71	    """text with every quoted span blanked out."""
72	    return QUOTED.sub(" ", text)
73	
74	
75	def spans(text):
76	    """The contents of each quoted span in text."""
77	    return [m.group(0)[1:-1] for m in QUOTED.finditer(text)]
78	
79	
80	def context(text, m, width=40):
81	    """About `width` characters around a match, so the offending sentence is findable."""
82	    return "..." + norm(text[max(0, m.start() - width // 2):m.end() + width // 2]) + "..."
83	
84	
85	def check_pronouns(audit):
86	    """(a) No third-person pronouns — except inside a verbatim quote in a source field."""
87	    fails = []
88	    for name, i, field, value in strings(audit):
89	        haystack = unquoted(value) if field.startswith("source") else value
90	        for m in PRONOUN.finditer(haystack):
91	            fails.append(f"{name}[{i}].{field}: pronoun {m.group(0)!r} in {context(haystack, m)}")
92	    return fails
93	
94	
95	def check_jargon(audit):
96	    """(b) Internal vocabulary must never reach the customer, quotes included."""
97	    fails = []
98	    for name, i, field, value in strings(audit):
99	        for pattern in JARGON:
100	            for m in pattern.finditer(value):
101	                fails.append(f"{name}[{i}].{field}: internal term {m.group(0)!r} in {context(value, m)}")
102	    return fails
103	
104	
105	_PROJECT_FILES = None
106	
107	
108	def project_files():
109	    """Basenames of files shipped with the project, excluding customer packets."""
110	    global _PROJECT_FILES
111	    if _PROJECT_FILES is None:
112	        _PROJECT_FILES = {p.name for p in (ROOT / "candidate").rglob("*")
113	                          if p.is_file() and "customer_packets" not in p.parts}
114	    return _PROJECT_FILES
115	
116	
117	def check_citations(audit, packet_dir):
118	    """(c) Every source citation names a real file, quotes it verbatim, and attributes it."""
119	    fails, cache = [], {}
120	    for name, i, field, value in strings(audit):
121	        if field not in CITED.get(name, ()):
122	            continue
123	        outside = unquoted(value)
124	        named = [f for f in FILENAME.findall(outside) if (packet_dir / f).is_file()]
125	        if not named:
126	            # A citation may legitimately point at a project file rather than a customer
127	            # document — the shipped schema, for instance, when explaining why something is
128	            # recorded in a particular shape. Those are pointers, not quotations of the
129	            # customer, so they are exempt from the verbatim and attribution rules. Every
130	            # other rule (pronouns, jargon) still applies to them.
131	            if any(f in project_files() for f in FILENAME.findall(outside)):
132	                continue
133	            fails.append(f"{name}[{i}].{field}: names no file in {packet_dir.name}/ "
134	                         f"and no file in the repo — {norm(value)[:70]!r}")
135	            continue
136	        if named[0] not in cache:
137	            cache[named[0]] = norm((packet_dir / named[0]).read_text())
138	        long_spans = [s for s in spans(value) if len(s.strip()) >= 15]
139	        if not long_spans:
140	            fails.append(f"{name}[{i}].{field}: no quoted span of 15+ characters — {norm(value)[:70]!r}")
141	        elif not any(norm(s) in cache[named[0]] for s in long_spans):
142	            fails.append(f"{name}[{i}].{field}: quote not verbatim in {named[0]} — {norm(long_spans[0])[:70]!r}")
143	        if not SPEAKER.search(outside) and not LOCATOR.search(outside):
144	            fails.append(f"{name}[{i}].{field}: no speaker name or row/line locator outside the "
145	                         f"quote (a timestamp alone is not attribution) — {norm(value)[:70]!r}")
146	    return fails
147	
148	
149	def check_flag_order(audit):
150	    """(d) Blocking flags first, so a reader who stops early has seen every blocker."""
151	    flags = audit.get("missing_information_flags") or []
152	    seen_non_blocking = None
153	    for i, flag in enumerate(flags):
154	        if not flag.get("blocking"):
155	            seen_non_blocking = i if seen_non_blocking is None else seen_non_blocking
156	        elif seen_non_blocking is not None:
157	            return [f"missing_information_flags[{i}] is blocking but follows non-blocking "
158	                    f"entry [{seen_non_blocking}] — move blocking flags first"]
159	    return []
160	
161	
162	def check_evidence(audit):
163	    """(e) Evidence must be present and dated — a bare assertion is not evidence."""
164	    fails = []
165	    for i, u in enumerate(audit.get("unsupported_api_requests") or []):
166	        ev = (u.get("evidence") or "").strip()
167	        if not ev:
168	            fails.append(f"unsupported_api_requests[{i}] has empty evidence")
169	        elif not YEAR.search(ev):
170	            fails.append(f"unsupported_api_requests[{i}] evidence carries no date: {ev[:60]!r}")
171	    return fails
172
